[3] Workbench/Code/Scripts.md (Scripts)
  - SilverBullet loads Space Lua scripts by priority, highest first.
[4] Virtual Pages.md (How it works)
  How it works: You define a virtual page by calling `virtualPage.define` with a Lua pattern and a function. When someone navigates to a page name matching the pattern, SilverBullet calls your function instead of loading a file from disk. / The current standard-library dispatcher passes the first captured value from the pattern to the function. The function returns the Markdown content to display. Put definitions in a `space-lua` block in your own space, then run `System: Reload`. / ```lua / virtualPage.define { / pattern = "greeting:(.+)", / run = function(name) / return "# Hello, " .. name .. "!\nWelcome to this virtual page." / end / } / ``` / Navigating to `greeting:World` renders a page with the heading “Hello, World!” — but no file is created. / Virtual pages are always **read-only**. The editor disables editing controls automatically.
[5] Architecture/Space Lua.md (Space Lua)
  [[Space Lua]] is SilverBullet’s embedded Lua dialect and runtime for extensions. It implements most of the Lua 5.4 standard library plus Space Lua-specific [[API]]s, and can reach all [[Architecture/Syscalls]].
[6] Space Lua/Quirks.md (Lua implementation notes)
  - Coroutines are missing from Space Lua; they are not planned because they are not useful in the SilverBullet context.
[7] Development.md (Stack)
  - At its most basic level, SilverBullet development can be done using Space Lua.
[8] Extensions.md (Libraries)
  - Space Lua is SilverBullet's embedded scripting language.
Exact facts:
- [1] SilverBullet lets users put dynamic content: live queries, computed views, templated rendering, and custom logic directly in their pages. In v1 this was spread across **three separate mechanisms**, each with its own syntax:
- [1] `space-lua` code blocks define space-wide functions and config.
- [1] Space Lua Integrated Query (SLIQ)** — `${query[[ from ... select ... ]]}` replaces the old query language. Because the body after `from` is a Lua expression, it can query the [[Object Index|object index]] *or* any Lua table.
